questionDecisions.holding: Treat the pardon route as available only when the operative clemency instrument expressly grants a **full pardon** of the conviction or convictions sought to be expunged.
The statewide statutory payment schedule controls:
AOC-497.2’s instruction to “check all that apply” is **disjunctive and charge-specific**.

Article 983(M)’s special **$300** first-offense marijuana fee schedule became “null, void, and without effect” on **August 1, 2026**. A motion filed after that date is governed by the ordinary Article 983 schedule unless another statutory exemption, fee waiver, or in-forma-pauperis mechanism applies.
More than one felony conviction may be expunged within a single ten-year period when **each conviction independently satisfies Article 978**.
questionDecisions.controllingProductDecision: Multiple felonies allowed if independently eligible

questionDecisions.holding: The better reading is that Article 985.3 authorizes discretionary **immediate expungement upon successful completion** of the qualifying court-ordered probation or alternative sentencing program and therefore displaces the ordinary five- and ten-year waiting clocks.
questionDecisions.reportDisposition: RELEASE — PACKET; contested timing to counsel

questionDecisions.holding: Use the official Article 989 motion **plus a supplemental redaction election**, rather than replacing the statewide motion with an entirely custom pleading.
Successful completion of a deferred disposition does **not automatically establish that the entire criminal-history record is confidential**.

The motion is filed in the underlying criminal case and the prosecutorial office that represented the State is entitled to notice. Current statute and forms do not clearly state that the clerk performs every initial service act.
The statute controls. A later conviction does **not** extinguish a sealing order entered under § 2262-A or § 2262-B.

Apply the same service rule as Q-009. The prosecutorial office is entitled to notice, and the current official materials do not justify promising that the court completes all participant-side service.
Section 610.130 sends the application to the court in which the person pleaded guilty or was sentenced, but the published case-type list provides no section-specific code.
LegalEase should not promise that one circuit court can expunge unrelated cases from multiple Missouri counties.
Failure by the prosecutor or judicial officer to provide subdivision (2)’s required notice does not eliminate the participant’s independent subdivision (1) remedy.
Participant copy must accurately separate the statute from the Judicial Branch procedure.
Route impaired-driving convictions exclusively through § 39-08-01.6.
Venue is the **district court of the county in which the arrest occurred**.
The county attorney is the respondent, and the petition must be served as a new civil action.
The candidate packet should contain more than the petition.
No statewide source establishes a filing fee for the motion filed in the existing Nebraska criminal case.
Nebraska’s in-forma-pauperis statute applies to civil or criminal cases, but the available official application forms do not fit an existing criminal case cleanly.
The same fee conclusion as Q-020 applies. The petition is filed in the sentencing criminal case, and no statewide published amount is established.
Use the custom criminal-case in-forma-pauperis application described in Q-021, not a mis-scoped civil checkbox form.

A conviction entered under a Nebraska Rules of the Road statute falls within the custodial-route mandatory-denial provision. A municipal ordinance conviction is not automatically a conviction “under” the state Rules merely because the local ordinance is substantively similar.
questionDecisions.controllingProductDecision: State Rules offense excluded; ordinance review

questionDecisions.holding: Same as Q-020 and Q-022. No statewide fee figure is established for the existing-case petition.
Same as Q-021 and Q-023. Use a custom criminal-case in-forma-pauperis affidavit/application and proposed order.
Route the participant to the circuit solicitor for the General Sessions nonconviction application.
Use the solicitor-administered application in the circuit of the offense. Section 17-1-65 is not one of the ordinary fee exemptions in § 17-22-940.

For a fingerprinted summary-court matter within § 17-22-950(A), the statute places a mandatory duty on the summary court. SCCA 223E is the subsection (B) application for the non-fingerprinted branch and should not be repurposed when the court simply failed to enter the automatic order.
Use the solicitor-administered application for a first eligible low-level conviction or qualifying third-degree domestic-violence conviction.

Section 22-5-910(E)’s same-incident rule affects **eligibility and conviction counting**, not the separate statutory rule governing which charges may be combined on one expungement order and one fee set.
questionDecisions.controllingProductDecision: Aggregation affects eligibility, not one order

questionDecisions.holding: Use the solicitor-administered Youthful Offender Act application in the circuit of the offense.
Use the solicitor-administered first-offense drug-conviction application.
Route by the **actual disposition**, not by the fact that the offense could have received a conditional discharge.
Use the circuit-solicitor application for the qualifying first-offense fraudulent-check conviction.
Use the circuit-solicitor application for the qualifying first-offense failure-to-stop-for-blue-light conviction.

Sealing under SDCL § 23A-27-17 is the court’s mandatory duty when a person is discharged and the matter dismissed under § 23A-27-14. There is no ordinary participant motion that triggers the initial sealing.
An absolute pardon based on innocence is implemented through a mandatory intergovernmental process, not a participant-filed expungement petition.
Section 19.2-392.12:1(B) creates a distinct participant petition for an ancillary matter after the underlying criminal charge or conviction has already been sealed by a qualifying mechanism.
Job-readiness graduation is an independent alternative to 90 days of treatment or recovery compliance, but the accelerated timing applies only to the statute’s **single-misdemeanor** branch.
questionDecisions.controllingProductDecision: Job-readiness is an OR trigger for single misdemeanor only

questionDecisions.holding: Current enacted text does not contain a residence-county venue option for multi-county conviction expungement.

The same conclusion as Q-041 applies. The statute supports grouping and disclosure of convictions by circuit court, but it does not name one receiving court for convictions spread across several circuits.
An excluded conviction should be omitted or severed rather than allowed to contaminate an otherwise eligible group.

questionDecisions.holding: A participant may legally file the published felony petition, but LegalEase cannot certify the central judicial findings in § 61-11-26(p)(5)(C)-(D).
Use **SCA-C906**, not the petition embedded in SCA-C900.
The current statute controls over the stale instruction sheet.
SCA-C903 is old but remains a workable official vehicle for a straightforward acquittal or dismissal that satisfies current § 61-11-25.
SCA-C903 alone is not the correct complete vehicle for a deferred-adjudication or diversion dismissal.
Section 5-1-16a(b) does not create a general “the event never occurred” rule or a universal right to deny the record to ordinary employers.
